concepts.title: Universal Law of Gravitation
concepts.body: The universal law of gravitation states that every object in the universe attracts every other object with a force that is directly proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them. For example, the Earth pulls you towards its center, keeping you grounded.

concepts.title: Free Fall and Acceleration Due to Gravity (g)
concepts.body: Free fall occurs when an object falls under the sole influence of gravity, experiencing an acceleration of about 9.8 m/s^2, which is the same for all masses. For instance, a feather and a hammer dropped in a vacuum will hit the ground simultaneously.

concepts.title: Mass vs Weight
concepts.body: Mass is the amount of matter in an object and remains constant everywhere, while weight is the force exerted on an object due to gravity and varies with the value of g. For example, your mass is the same on Earth and the Moon, but your weight is less on the Moon.

formulas.title: Universal Gravitational Force
formulas.body: F = G x m1 x m2 / r^2 (F in newton N, m in kg, r in m, G = 6.67 x 10^-11 N m^2/kg^2). This formula calculates the gravitational force between two objects, where G is the gravitational constant, m1 and m2 are the masses of the objects, and r is the distance between their centers.

formulas.title: Weight
formulas.body: W = m x g (W in newton N, m in kg, g in m/s^2). This formula calculates the weight of an object, where m is its mass and g is the acceleration due to gravity.

examples.title: Everyday Example
examples.body: When you jump, you eventually come back to the ground because of Earth's gravitational pull. The cause is the gravitational force acting between you and the Earth.

examples.title: Applied Example
examples.body: Satellites orbit the Earth due to the gravitational force between them and the Earth. The cause is the centripetal force provided by gravity, which keeps the satellite in its path.

mcqs.question: What is the value of acceleration due to gravity (g) on Earth?
mcqs.explanation: The acceleration due to gravity on Earth is approximately 9.8 m/s^2. The other options are incorrect as they do not match the standard value.

mcqs.question: If the mass of an object is 10 kg, what is its weight on Earth?
mcqs.explanation: Weight is calculated using W = m x g. Here, m = 10 kg and g = 9.8 m/s^2, so W = 10 x 9.8 = 98 N. The other options are incorrect because they either use the wrong value of g or m.

mcqs.question: Two objects of masses 5 kg and 10 kg are placed 2 m apart. What is the gravitational force between them?
mcqs.explanation: Using F = G x m1 x m2 / r^2, where G = 6.67 x 10^-11 N m^2/kg^2, m1 = 5 kg, m2 = 10 kg, and r = 2 m, F = 6.67 x 10^-11 x 5 x 10 / 4 = 3.34 x 10^-9 N. The other options are incorrect because they either use the wrong values or miscalculate the force.
